title: Initial-configuration language characterization
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $S,c$ be natural numbers. The encoding of $x$, $c$, and $S$ belongs to the initial-configuration language of $N$ if and only if $c$ equals the code, at space bound $S$, of the initial configuration of $N$ on input $x$.
